findings.message: The deprecated `--track-id` compatibility argument was previously ignored on a track branch by `resolve_pr_branch`, but the interactor now rejects any value that is not a valid `TrackId` before reaching the port. Commands such as `pr push --track-id INVALID` therefore change from operating on the current track to exiting with failure, violating CN-01. Preserve the ignored compatibility semantics when constructing the typed command.

`NonEmptyString::try_new` trims its input, so an explicit base such as `" main "` is silently changed to `"main"`. The baseline treated only the exactly empty string as omitted and otherwise forwarded the value unchanged; this can now create a PR against a different base instead of failing, contrary to CN-01. Use a non-trimming representation for this override.

The new public validation branches lack the required error-case coverage: only `status` with an empty identifier is tested, while invalid/compatibility track IDs, explicit-base boundaries, invalid merge methods and timestamps, and empty identifiers for wait/trigger/poll are untested. Add focused regression tests for these public service paths.

The usecase catalogue references `PrCommandOutput` and `SignalCommandOutput` in `PrCommandPort.execute` and `SignalCommandPort.execute`, but neither output type is declared in any of the six in-scope catalogues. This leaves the secondary-port contract without a declared return type/shape and omits the post-change public types that the drivers and adapters consume.

`PrCommandPort::execute` performs filesystem, Git/GitHub, terminal, and polling I/O through `SystemPrCommandAdapter`, but is declared synchronous and the entry docs do not acknowledge an intentional blocking/synchronous CLI boundary. Document that choice or make the port async to avoid adapter-level color rework.

`SignalCommandPort::execute` covers filesystem, Git, rustdoc, and gate I/O through `SystemSignalCommandAdapter`, but is declared synchronous without docs establishing that blocking execution is intentional. Document the synchronous CLI model or expose an async contract.

`usecase::PrCommand` crosses the public `PrCommandPort::execute` boundary, so secondary-adapter consumers must match its variants, but the entry does not state whether the variant set is intentionally closed or extension-tolerant (`#[non_exhaustive]`). Record the intended enum evolution policy.

`usecase::PrReviewCycleMode` is a public payload consumed by `PrCommandPort` adapters, but its entry does not explicitly establish closed/exhaustive versus extension-tolerant matching semantics. Record the intended enum evolution policy.

`usecase::SignalCommand` crosses the public `SignalCommandPort::execute` boundary, requiring secondary adapters to match its variants, but the entry does not state whether the nine-variant set is intentionally closed or extension-tolerant (`#[non_exhaustive]`). Record the intended enum evolution policy.

GO-01 is not fully covered: AC-03 verifies the driver → usecase interactor → port pure-DI path only for PR, while no acceptance criterion deterministically verifies the equivalent Signal execution path. AC-02 and AC-04 only constrain the Signal composition root and legacy references, so a Signal path that still bypasses the intended typed DI route could satisfy all current ACs.

findings.message: The two `contains` checks do not freeze the stdout contract: extra lines, changed ordering, or other output regressions still pass. AC-05 requires stdout parity, so assert the complete expected byte sequence.

The Git setup helpers and the `sotp` child inherit system/global Git configuration and Git-related environment variables. Settings such as `commit.gpgSign`, `core.hooksPath`, or URL rewrites can break or redirect this test; isolate Git configuration consistently for every spawned process.

Only the successful push contract is covered. A regression that maps a failed push to a successful exit code or the wrong stderr stream would remain undetected; add a deterministic failure scenario asserting non-zero exit, stderr, and absence of the remote ref.

The Git subprocesses inherit the developer/CI machine's global and system Git configuration. For example, `commit.gpgSign=true` can make the fixture commit fail, while `core.hooksPath`, push signing, or URL rewrites can change or fail the exercised `pr push`. Isolate Git configuration for both the fixture commands and `sotp` (for example with `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM`, an empty `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, and cleared inherited Git overrides).

The two `contains` assertions do not preserve the stdout contract required by AC-05: additional output or reversed message order would still pass. Assert the complete expected stdout, including ordering and newlines, so observable output regressions are detected.

`trigger_state_path` silently falls back to an empty `PathBuf` when `SystemGitRepo::discover()` fails, causing trigger state to be read or written relative to the process working directory. This can persist PR review state outside the repository (or load unrelated state) instead of failing closed; propagate repository-discovery errors through `Result` and map them to the adapter error.

`cleanup_trigger_state` discards `remove_file` errors. After a successful review cycle, failure to delete the persisted trigger state leaves stale state that can be consumed by a later resume operation, potentially resuming the wrong PR review cycle. Propagate or explicitly surface cleanup failures.

`save_trigger_state` writes `tmp/pr-review-state/<track>.json` without rejecting symlinks in the parent path or at the leaf; load and cleanup reuse the same unguarded path. A tracked or pre-created symlink can redirect state I/O outside the repository and overwrite or delete arbitrary same-user files. Apply the fail-closed `reject_symlinks_below`/`symlink_metadata` pattern before every access and add symlink-rejection tests.

`resume_trigger_state` discards `resolve_head()` errors as `None` and skips the saved/current HEAD comparison; `trigger_new_review` similarly persists `None`. A transient git-adapter failure therefore disables stale-review protection, allowing resume after HEAD changes. Propagate resolution failures and require a HEAD after the cycle has pushed its branch.

This unit test changes the process-global current directory while Rust tests run in parallel. Concurrent infrastructure tests using `SystemGitRepo::discover()` can observe this temporary repository and fail nondeterministically or operate on the wrong fixture. Use a subprocess or injected root, or coordinate through a crate-wide lock shared by all CWD-mutating tests.

`trigger_state_location` interpolates an unvalidated raw track ID into a repository-root path, while `guard_trigger_state_path` checks only symlinks and never rejects `ParentDir`/path prefixes or verifies normalized containment under `root`. This is not fail-closed if a non-domain track ID reaches the helper. Validate with `TrackId` and enforce the `is_safe_briefing_path`-style trusted-root containment check before any I/O.

`trigger_new_review` posts the external `@codex review` comment before the newly fallible `resolve_head_hash` call. If HEAD resolution fails, the command returns failure without saving trigger state, so `--resume` cannot recover and retrying posts a duplicate review. Resolve HEAD before posting, or otherwise persist a recoverable post-success state on subsequent failures.
